subject: Dedicated footprint request — SLO curve, burst profile, and session mix
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@qubitai.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@qubitai.com>, procurement@qubitai.com
Date: 2029-08-01T08:12:00Z
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — early workload snapshot

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We're very close to committing to a reserved footprint if the economics and SLA align. To help our procurement and infra teams, can you provide dedicated sizing guidance for a pilot + production ramp? I've attached a short CSV with per-endpoint sample rates and a one-page summary. High-level notes below — we can fill more detail as requested:

- Product: QubitAssist (multimodal assistant for developer docs)
- Expected user-facing qps at pilot: 120 rps peak, production (6 months): 900 rps peak with ~15 min bursts
- Mixed workloads: 70% short completion (chat: 80–200 tokens out), 25% long generation (200–800 tokens), 5% embeddings/batch-indexing
- Prompt lengths: median 120 tokens, 95th percentile 420 tokens (including context history)
- Response lengths: median 140 tokens, 95th percentile 700 tokens
- Session behavior: chat sessions reuse KV cache for ~6 turns on average; 10% of sessions are long-running (> 20 turns)
- Latency SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 250ms for chat; p99 targets depend on model mix but we want guidance for p99/p995
- Preferred GPU: H100 if cost-effective, but open to A100p and mixed-quantized variants

Questions we need answered for procurement:
1) Preliminary GPU mix to meet p95/p99 targets given the above mix and a target of 99.9% uptime SLA
2) Burst handling: how Redis/queueing + reserved capacity interacts with 15-min bursts and expected warmup costs
3) Token-econ estimate (approx $/1k tokens) for recommended config and batch/oversubscription assumptions
4) Any constraints around session cache retention and concurrency limits we should account for in product design

Can you use the attached CSV as a starting point and tell us what additional telemetry you need? Happy to hop on a short session if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform
QubitAI

Attachment: qubitai_workload_summary.csv (4KB)
From: camila_reyes@redwood.com
To: Alex Morgan <alex@qubitai.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@qubitai.com>, procurement@qubitai.com
Date: 2029-08-01T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — early workload snapshot

Alex — thanks for the detailed snapshot, this is exactly the kind of input we need to start a territory-specific sizing. I've attached our quick "Dedicated Sizer" workbook (redwood-dedicated-sizer-form.xlsx) and a short mutual action plan you can share with procurement.

Quick clarifying items before we model: could you confirm the following (answers inline are fine):
- Model(s) you expect to serve (open models / LLM family and approximate parameters)
- Expected fraction of requests that will be streamed (server-sent tokens) vs single-response blocking calls
- Acceptable p99 and p995 latency windows (you gave p95 targets; we need p99/p995 to size for tail with burst headroom)
- Warmup behavior: do you plan to pre-warm sessions at the start of business hours or rely solely on on-demand cold starts?
- KV cache reuse hit-rate estimate (you said 6 turns; an approximate percent hit-rate helps)

I'll run the numbers assuming a mixed model profile (1x large generation model + smaller chat model) and produce:
- Recommended GPU mix (H100/A100/4xA10 alternatives)
- Occupancy-based concurrency limits and conservative oversubscription suggestions
- Estimated token cost ranges for pilot vs production (with batching assumptions)
- A suggested canary and burst-handling playbook (how to use reserved + burst capacity + fallback smaller model)

If you can return the filled sizer or reply inline with the bullets, I'll get a first-cut sizing and a short slide summary by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizer-form.xlsx, qai-mup-action-plan.docx
From: Alex Morgan <alex@qubitai.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@qubitai.com>, procurement@qubitai.com
Date: 2029-08-01T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — early workload snapshot

Camila — thanks, attached is a quick fill of the sizer and a few notes inline below (I also uploaded the CSV to the Drive link).

Inline answers:
- Models: primary gen model is a 70B open decoder (quantized to 4/8-bit in some paths); fallback/assistant is a 13B chat-tuned model.
- Streamed responses: ~30% of long generations will be streamed; short chat replies usually return as a single chunk
- p99/p995 targets: p99 < 500ms, p995 < 900ms for chat paths; for long generations we accept p99 < 1200ms if using streaming
- Warmup: we'll pre-warm a small portion of sessions at the start of business hours (target 20% pre-warmed), rest are on-demand
- KV hit-rate: ~62% average across sessions; long-running sessions have ~85% reuse within the session window

Quick numbers from the sizer (pilot -> production):
- Pilot peak (120 rps): ~6 H100-equivalent GPUs with conservative occupancy (no oversubscription) to hit p99 targets for chat
- Production peak (900 rps, 15-min bursts): rough starting point is 40 H100-equivalent GPUs with occupancy tuned to 70% for steady state and burst headroom reserved separately
- Token mix: avg request 260 tokens (prompt+response), peak batch windows push token throughput ~2.4M tokens/min during bursts
- Expected batch/oversubscription: pilot: minimal batching (real-time chat), prod: batching for long gens + 1.5x logical oversubscription for embeddings jobs

I've attached qubitai_workload_summary.csv and the filled sizer. Let me know if you want a short 30-min sizing review tomorrow.

Cheers,
Alex
